newsitem.title: GERMANY: Juncker-significant number of lands for EMU in 97.
newsitem.headline: Juncker-significant number of lands for EMU in 97.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said on Thursday that he thought a "signficant" number of countries would meet the criteria for European monetary union.
He said the budget deficit criteria in the Maastricht treaty, which requires would-be members to limit their budget deficits to three percent of GDP, should be read as three percent, not 3.0 percent.

"The three in the (Maastricht treaty) should be interpreted in terms of trend," Juncker said in Bonn. "If (German finance minister) Theo Waigel had said 3.8 (percent) was also okay, countries would never have made the strict effort."

Juncker said he thought the European Central Bank (ECB), which is officially due to take over the operations of the European Monetary Institute when the euro starts in 1999, must be an independent body.
He also said a stability pact was necessary, but it did not mean job losses and there was no contradiction between good fiscal policy and a serious labour market policy.

Juncker also praised Spain and Italy for their efforts to meet the EMU criteria. He said that contrary to the views of some people, Spain and Italy had made much greater efforts to meet the EMU goals than others in Europe.
